title: A Remastered graphics preset above High: first pass
summary: Settings → Display → Graphics has a fifth choice, Remastered. It adds sun relief to the terrain, a soft glow and film grade over the frame, wind in nearby plants and sun glint on water. It is opt-in: Auto never picks it, and Original, Enhanced and High draw exactly as before.
details: The original terrain is unlit. Remastered shades it from each venue's own sun: slopes facing the sun brighten and warm, slopes facing away darken, and flat ground keeps its authored brightness.

A finish pass adds bloom from the brightest parts of the frame, a small exposure lift, a highlight roll-off, a little more colour, a light vignette and dither. The frame stays 8-bit, so it runs on WebGL2.
Nearby plant meshes lean in a gusting wind, and the venue's sun glints off the water's waves.

Checked on one Mac: Original, Enhanced and High captures on two venues are byte-identical to a build from before the change; the browser test draws Remastered on WebGL2 without errors and the settings test cycles through it.
limitation: Nothing but vehicles casts shadows yet; world shadows from terrain, scenery and trees are the next step. Split screen skips the glow and grade. Tuned on host captures of ten venues only: no phone test and no frame-time measurement yet.
verification: Host only, one Mac (Metal natively, WebGL2 in Chromium): Original, Enhanced and High captures at 960×540 on env01 and env05 are byte-identical to the previous build. tools/test_engine_remastered.mjs and tools/test_engine_settings.mjs pass.
caption: High (left) and Remastered (right): the sunlit hill gains relief and the sky glows.
